concept.name: Forced liquidation
concept.definition: The mandatory closing of a position by the broker, clearinghouse, or exchange without the holder's consent, triggered when account equity falls below the maintenance margin and margin calls are not — or cannot be — met.
concept.intuition: When you can't or won't post more collateral, the venue closes the trade for you, at whatever price the market gives, to stop the loss from eating other people's money.
concept.mechanics: Once equity breaches maintenance margin, the liquidation process takes over: on futures venues the position may be liquidated automatically, and on crypto venues a laddered process first reduces the position to lower risk tiers. Any residual loss beyond the bankruptcy price passes to the insurance fund or, failing that, to auto-deleveraging.
concept.formula: Trigger condition: account equity < maintenance margin requirement for the open position, with equity computed at the mark price.
concept.failure_modes: Forced selling is pro-cyclical: cascades of liquidations push prices further, triggering more liquidations in a spiral, and fills occur at distressed prices with maximal slippage. In extreme moves the engine can fail to close above the bankruptcy price, creating bad debt.
concept.misconceptions: Forced liquidation is not a penalty or fee event — it is a risk-control mechanism — and the trader chooses neither timing nor price; partial liquidation to a lower tier can precede full liquidation, so it is not always all-or-nothing.
concept.example: An account whose balance falls below maintenance margin and cannot meet the call has its futures position liquidated automatically, as CME's margin rules describe; on crypto venues the engine reduces the position tier by tier before full close-out.
